name: Pastir Luka
speaker: young-man

title.en: Luka checks the sheep in the fold
title.de: Luka schaut nach den Schafen im Pferch

personality: Young shepherd, nineteen, from a farm on the Trnovo plateau. Cheerful, a little absent-minded, shouts across valleys, talks to his sheep by name (Bela, Črna, Pikica). Short sentences, lots of 'ej!' and 'veš', says ti at once and likes it back. Loves the mountains and the burja; hates fog, because the sheep get lost in it.
story: Luka grazes the village's sheep on the meadow below the forest and takes them up to the plateau in summer. Bela, the white one, keeps getting lost, and every dog in Trnovo knows his whistle. His dream is a hut of his own up on the plateau.

likes.it: la bora (il vento freddo da nord-est)

greet.en: Hey, hi! Are you the new one?
greet.de: He, hallo! Bist du {m:der Neue|f:die Neue}?
greet.it: Ehi, ciao! Sei tu {m:il nuovo|f:la nuova}?

greet.en: Hi! I am Luka. The shepherd.
greet.de: Hallo! Ich bin Luka. Der Hirte.

greet.en: {learner}! Just in time. Have you seen Bela?
greet.de: {learner}! Gerade recht. Hast du Bela gesehen?

greet.sl: Ej, {learner}, {m:prijatelj|f:prijateljica}! Pridi, ovce te že poznajo.
greet.en: Hey, {learner}, my friend! Come, the sheep know you already.
greet.de: He, {learner}, {m:mein Freund|f:meine Freundin}! Komm, die Schafe kennen dich schon.
greet.it: Ehi, {learner}, {m:amico mio|f:amica mia}! Vieni, le pecore ti conoscono già.

greet.en: {learner}! {m:Brother|f:Girl}! Today we two go up to the pasture, yes?
greet.de: {learner}! {m:Bruder|f:Mädel}! Heute gehen wir zwei auf die Alm, ja?
greet.it: {learner}! {m:Fratello|f:Ragazza}! Oggi noi due saliamo al pascolo, sì?

thanks.en: Thank you, you really helped me.
thanks.de: Danke dir, du hast mir echt geholfen.

thanks.sl: Ej, hvala! Brez tebe bi Bela še zdaj tavala.
thanks.en: Hey, thanks! Without you Bela would still be wandering.
thanks.de: He, danke! Ohne dich würde Bela jetzt noch herumirren.
thanks.it: Ehi, grazie! Senza di te Bela starebbe ancora vagando.

remember.sl: Ej, veš, še vedno mislim na {memory}!
remember.en: Hey, you know, I still think of {memory}!
remember.de: He, weißt du, ich denke noch oft an {memory}!

remember.sl: Ko sem sam na planini, mislim na {memory}.
remember.en: When I am alone on the pasture, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich allein auf der Alm bin, denke ich an {memory}.
remember.it: Quando sono solo al pascolo, ricordo {memory}.

idle.sl: Bela je spet nekje v gozdu.
idle.en: Bela is somewhere in the forest again.
idle.de: Bela ist wieder irgendwo im Wald.
idle.it: Bela è di nuovo da qualche parte nel bosco.

idle.sl: Slišiš zvonce? Tam so, za smrekami.
idle.en: Can you hear the bells? They are there, behind the spruces.
idle.de: Hörst du die Glocken? Da sind sie, hinter den Fichten.
idle.it: Senti i campanacci? Sono là, dietro gli abeti.

idle.sl: Burja piha. Danes bo mrzlo, veš.
idle.en: The burja is blowing. It will be cold today, you know.
idle.de: Die Bora weht. Heute wird's kalt, weißt du.
idle.it: Soffia la bora. Oggi farà freddo, sai.

comfort.it: Non fa niente. Ancora una volta!

comfort.sl: Ah, ni panike. Tudi Bela se izgubi.
comfort.en: Ah, no panic. Bela gets lost too.
comfort.de: Ach, keine Panik. Bela verläuft sich auch.
comfort.it: Ah, niente panico. Anche Bela si perde.

bye.en: Bye, {learner}! I'm off to get the sheep. (čav: Primorska for bye)
bye.de: Tschüss, {learner}! Ich hol die Schafe. (čav: so sagt man in Primorska tschüss)
bye.it: Ciao, {learner}! Vado a prendere le pecore. (čav: il ciao della Primorska)

bye.en: See you! Watch out for the burja.
bye.de: Bis bald! Pass auf die Bora auf.

liked.sl: Ej, {learner}! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}? To imam res rad!
liked.en: Hey, {learner}! How did you know? I really like this!
liked.de: He, {learner}! Woher wusstest du das? Das mag ich echt!
liked.it: Ehi, {learner}! Come lo sapevi? Questo mi piace un sacco!

liked.sl: Zame? Super! Bela, poglej, kaj mi je dal {learner}!
liked.en: For me? Great! Bela, look what {learner} gave me!
liked.de: Für mich? Super! Bela, schau, was {learner} mir geschenkt hat!
liked.it: Per me? Forte! Bela, guarda cosa mi ha regalato {learner}!

liked.sl: Ej, hvala, {m:prijatelj|f:prijateljica}! Točno to rabim na planini.
liked.en: Hey, thanks, friend! Exactly what I need up on the pasture.
liked.de: He, danke, {m:Freund|f:Freundin}! Genau das brauche ich auf der Alm.
liked.it: Ehi, grazie, {m:amico|f:amica}! Proprio quello che mi serve al pascolo.

ordinary.en: Hey, thanks, {learner}! That's nice of you.
ordinary.it: Ehi, grazie, {learner}! Gentile da parte tua.

ordinary.sl: O, hvala! Ni treba, veš. Ampak hvala.
ordinary.en: Oh, thanks! You don't have to, you know. But thanks.
ordinary.de: Oh, danke! Das wäre nicht nötig gewesen, weißt du. Aber danke.
ordinary.it: Oh, grazie! Non dovevi, sai. Ma grazie.

rare.sl: Ej, ej, ej! Tega pa še nisem imel! Hvala, {m:brat|f:punca}!
rare.en: Hey, hey, hey! I've never had this! Thanks, {m:brother|f:girl}!
rare.de: He, he, he! So was hatte ich noch nie! Danke, {m:Bruder|f:Mädel}!
rare.it: Ehi, ehi, ehi! Una cosa così non l'ho mai avuta! Grazie, {m:fratello|f:ragazza}!
